heroHeadline: Sept 19-20: SpaceX Launches Starlink 15-27 (109th of 2026), SPCX Closes at $152.71 Ahead of Monday's Nasdaq-100 Reweighting
heroSubtitle: 8,903 days since SpaceX founding — SpaceX launched 27 Starlink V2 Mini satellites from Vandenberg SLC-4E at 6:47pm PDT Sept 19 (01:47 UTC Sept 20), its 109th Falcon-family launch and 81st Starlink mission of 2026; booster B1093 flew its 17th mission and landed on the 'Of Course I Still Love You' droneship, its 225th recovery on that vessel. SPCX shares closed at $152.71 on Sept 18 (-$2.10, -1.36%) from Sept 17's $154.81, as the Nasdaq-100's quarterly rebalance trades executed at that close, lifting SpaceX's index weighting to roughly 2.82% from about 1.28% — an estimated $15.5-22 billion in net passive-fund buying — with the new weighting taking effect at Sept 21's market open. Markets were closed over the weekend; no new trading data for Sept 19-20. Starship Flight 14, the program's first attempt at full orbital insertion, remains targeted for no earlier than Sept 28 from Starbase.
